My immediate instinct is to take a high-level view of this "Campfire" codebase. Before I even think about specific functionalities or changes, I need to get a mental map. I'm going to start by understanding the architecture, the basic file structure, and how everything is organized. I'm looking for the obvious key directories – how are the bot implementations handled? Where are mentions processed? What about the webhooks; where do they live? How are jobs scheduled and managed? And of course, messages and routes: I want to see how these fundamental parts work in coordination. I will examine the testing methodology as well – how thoroughly are these areas covered? This broad overview will be crucial before I dive into any specific area.

# Chat Bots Architecture

## Data Model
Bots are `User` records with `role: :bot` (`User::Role`), implemented via the `User::Bot` concern:
- `users.bot_token`: unique random token (`SecureRandom.base58(24)`) generated on create for bots; `nil` for human users and deactivated bots.
- `users.creator_id`: references the `User` who created the bot, allowing `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)` to work uniformly for creators and administrators.
- `bot_key` (`"<id>-<bot_token>"`): the credential displayed in the UI ("Bot code") and used in the messaging API URL. Verified with `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Reusing `User` means bots automatically inherit:
  - Open-room auto-join (`after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms` and `Rooms::Open`)
  - Closed-room membership management (`Rooms::ClosedsController`)
  - Message authorship (`messages.creator_id`), avatars (`User::Avatar`), broadcasts (`Message::Broadcasts`), and push notifications (`Room::MessagePusher`)
- Bots are excluded from human-only surfaces (login, session transfers, account member list, sidebar DM placeholders) via `User.not_bot`.
- Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate`, which sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token: nil`, and removes all memberships while preserving historical messages.

## Routes & Controllers
- `BotsController` (`resources :bots, except: :show`): UI for listing (`/bots`), creating (`/bots/new`), editing (`/bots/:id/edit`), and deleting bots. Linked from `/account/edit` ("Set up chat bots") for all members.
- `Bots::MessagesController` (`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages`): unauthenticated, CSRF-exempt endpoint reading raw request body (or `params[:attachment]`) and returning `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`, `422 Unprocessable Content`, `404 Not Found`, or `401 Unauthorized`.

require "test_helper"

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "creating a bot generates a bot token and grants membership to open rooms" do
    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, +Rooms::Open.count do
      @bot = User.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_equal "#{@bot.id}-#{@bot.bot_token}", @bot.bot_key
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.order(:id).pluck(:id), @bot.rooms.order(:id).pluck(:id)
  end

  test "bot requires a name" do
    bot = User.new(name: "", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert bot.errors[:name].any?
  end

  test "authenticate_bot validates active bots with matching key" do
    bot = User.create!(name: "CI Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_equal bot, User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}-wrongtoken")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("999999-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("invalid")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(nil)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{users(:david).id}-")
  end

  test "deactivating a bot revokes memberships and invalidates bot_key while preserving messages" do
    bot = User.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_nil bot.bot_key

  end
end

class RoomsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ show destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ destroy ]
  before_action :remember_last_room_visited, only: :show

  def index
    redirect_to room_url(Current.user.rooms.last)
  end

  def show
    @messages = find_messages
  end

  def destroy
    @room.destroy

    broadcast_remove_room
    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_room
      if room = room_scope.find_by(id: params[:room_id] || params[:id])
        @room = room
      else
        redirect_to root_url, alert: "Room not found or inaccessible"
      end
    end

    # Subclasses narrow this to the room types they're allowed to act on, so that one
    # room namespace can't be used to reach another's rooms.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@room)
    end

    def ensure_permission_to_create_rooms
      if Current.account.settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators? && !Current.user.administrator?
        head :forbidden
      end
    end

    def find_messages
      messages = @room.messages.with_creator.with_attachment_details.with_boosts

      if show_first_message = messages.find_by(id: params[:message_id])
        @messages = messages.page_around(show_first_message)
      else
        @messages = messages.last_page
      end
    end

    def room_params
      params.require(:room).permit(:name)
    end

    def broadcast_remove_room
      broadcast_remove_to :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ]
    end
end

**Analyzing Webhook URL Validation in Campfire**

Okay, so I've hit a key insight regarding `RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard` – if we used it, QA tests running Campfire in Docker or locally could be blocked from using mock webhooks on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or other private IPs. That's a huge problem. Especially since Campfire bots are *designed* to integrate with internal services, CI, and local scripts. And the prompt *didn't* mention any requirement to block private IPs, which is a key consideration.

Let's re-examine this. What's the best approach for webhook URL validation, if we don't want to restrict private networks? The prompt *does* concern itself with URL validation, so if a `webhook_url` is provided, we should ensure it's a valid `URI::HTTP` which makes sense (prevents `javascript:` or malformed URLs), while explicitly *allowing* `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, private IPs, and public URLs! 

So, I could use: `uri = URI.parse(webhook_url); uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present?`. I need to ensure I handle both `http://` and `https://` protocols, so `URI::HTTPS` being a subclass of `URI::HTTP` is perfect for that. I should also handle potentially malformed URLs and invalid schemes.

We also have to think about whitespace! Stripping whitespace (`url.strip.presence`) from the URL handles spaces and sets it to `nil` if there's only whitespace. What if someone enters an empty string, like `""`, for the `webhook_url`? It could be the user wants to remove the webhook. If the model normalizes the URL by removing leading/trailing whitespace, a blank submission means that field is set to `nil`.

Now, let's consider bot deactivation. Should we also clear the `webhook_url` when a bot is deactivated? Or does the deactivation status prevent webhook firing? A deactivated bot is removed from memberships, and `User.active` won't include it. We should also check `bot.active?` before firing any webhook. Checking `bot.active? && bot.webhook_url.present?` is a great idea, but clearing `webhook_url: nil` on deactivation would be a clean and explicit choice (like `bot_token: nil`).

Finally, I need to check the configuration files for ActiveJob, Resque, etc., to see how they're set up within the application.

**Webhook URL Validation and Payload Analysis**

Okay, first things first, Campfire uses HTML5 validation and/or `unprocessable_content` responses. Now, the main concern here is making sure that a bad `webhook_url` doesn't cause any problems. If the user submits a bad URL, say `"not a url"`, `"ftp://example.com"`, or `"javascript:alert(1)"`, the app needs to handle it gracefully. My focus is going to be on the `User::Bot` model. I'll need to check the normalization and validation methods specifically.

Looking at the code, it normalizes the URL by stripping whitespace and allowing a `nil` value, which is good. Then the existing validation uses `URI::DEFAULT_PARSER.make_regexp(%w[http https])`. I need to ensure the matching is correct – it needs to match correctly and not cause false positives or negatives. Oh wait! It's unanchored! That means something like `"foo http://bar"` would pass, which is bad! I'll need a custom validator with `URI.parse` to ensure a *valid* URL with a host, e.g. a custom validator.

Now, let's trace this validation step by step:
*   `nil` is valid (optional).
*   Empty string or whitespace will be normalized to `nil`, valid too (removes the bot's webhook, nice).
*   `"https://example.com/hook"` -> `URI::HTTPS`, with a host, so it's all good.
*   `"http://localhost:4567/webhook"` -> `URI::HTTP`, with a host, so it's also good.
*   `"http://127.0.0.1:8080/bot"` -> `URI::HTTP`, has host, so valid.
*   `"ftp://example.com"` -> not `URI::HTTP` -> invalid.
*   `"javascript:alert(1)"` -> not `URI::HTTP` -> invalid.
*   `"not a url"` -> `URI::InvalidURIError` -> invalid.

Okay, that's the validation part taken care of. I don't want to get distracted with any non-critical features, for example, displaying the URL on `bots/index`. The prompt said only to add the field, not to change anything else. So I'll just leave `bots/index` alone to avoid breaking anything.

4.  `message`:
    *   `"id"`: `message.id`. Simple enough.
    *   `"link"`: `Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_at_message_path(room, message)`. This translates to `"/rooms/#{room.id}/@#{message.id}"`. And I need to verify that `RoomsController#show` handles this `@:message_id` with `params[:message_id]` properly. The code in `RoomsController#find_messages` confirms it does.
    *   `"body"`:

class ContentFilters::RemoveSoloUnfurledLinkText < ActionText::Content::Filter
  def applicable?
    normalize_tweet_url(solo_unfurled_url) == normalize_tweet_url(content.to_plain_text)
  end

  def apply
    fragment.replace("div") { |node| node.tap { |n| n.inner_html = unfurled_links.first.to_s } }
  end

  private
    TWITTER_DOMAINS = %w[ x.com twitter.com ]
    TWITTER_DOMAIN_MAPPING = { "x.com" => "twitter.com" }

    def solo_unfurled_url
      unfurled_links.first["href"] if unfurled_links.size == 1
    end

    def unfurled_links
      fragment.find_all("action-text-attachment[@content-type='#{ActionText::Attachment::OpengraphEmbed::OPENGRAPH_EMBED_CONTENT_TYPE}']")
    end

    def normalize_tweet_url(url)
      return url unless twitter_url?(url)

      uri = URI.parse(url)

      uri.dup.tap do |u|
        u.host = TWITTER_DOMAIN_MAPPING[uri.host&.downcase] || uri.host
        u.query = nil
      end.to_s
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      url
    end

    def twitter_url?(url)
      url.present? && TWITTER_DOMAINS.any? { |domain| url.strip.include?(domain) }
    end
end

require "net/http"

class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5.seconds
  READ_TIMEOUT = 10.seconds

  attr_reader :bot, :message

  def initialize(bot:, message:)
    @bot = bot
    @message = message
  end

  def deliver
    return unless deliverable?

    response = post_payload
    handle_response(response)
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.warn "Failed to deliver webhook for bot #{bot.id} to #{bot.webhook_url} (#{e.class}: #{e.message})"
  end

  private
    def deliverable?
      bot.active? && bot.bot? && bot.webhook_url.present? && bot.rooms.exists?(message.room_id)
    end

    def post_payload
      uri = URI.parse(bot.webhook_url)
      request = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri)
      request["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
      request.body = payload.to_json

      Net::HTTP.start(
        uri.host,
        uri.port,
        use_ssl: uri.scheme == "https",
        open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT,
        read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT
      ) do |http|
        http.request(request)
      end
    end

    def handle_response(response)
      return unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK)

      reply_body = extract_reply_body(response)
      return if reply_body.blank?

      reply_message = message.room.messages.create!(body: reply_body, creator: bot)
      reply_message.broadcast_create
    end

    def extract_reply_body(response)
      raw = response.body.to_s.dup.force_encoding("UTF-8").scrub
      return if raw.blank?

      case response.content_type&.downcase
      when "text/plain"
        ERB::Util.html_escape(raw)
      when "text/html"
        raw
      end
    end

    def payload
      routes = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers
      room = message.room

      {
        event: "mention",
        author: {
          id: message.creator.id,
          name: message.creator.name
        },
        room: {
          id: room.id,
          name: room_name(room),
          reply_to: routes.room_bot_messages_path(room, bot.bot_key)
        },
        message: {
          id: message.id,
          body: {
            text: stripped_plain_text,
            html: message.body.to_s
          },
          link: routes.room_at_message_path(room, message)
        }
      }
    end

    def room_name(room)
      room.name.presence || room.users.without(bot).pluck(:name).to_sentence.presence
    end

    def stripped_plain_text
      return "" unless message.body.body

      sentinel = "__CAMPFIRE_MENTION_#{SecureRandom.hex(8)}__"
      replaced_fragment = message.body.body.fragment.replace("action-text-attachment") do |node|
        ActionText::Attachment.from_node(node).attachable == bot ? sentinel : node
      end

      ActionText::Content.new(replaced_fragment).to_plain_text
        .gsub(/[^\S\n]*#{sentinel}[^\S\n]*/) { |match|
          match.match?(/\A[^\S\n]/) && match.match?(/[^\S\n]\z/) ? " " : ""
        }
        .strip
    end
end
EOF

require "net/http"

class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5.seconds
  READ_TIMEOUT = 10.seconds

  attr_reader :bot, :message

  def initialize(bot:, message:)
    @bot = bot
    @message = message
  end

  def deliver
    return unless deliverable?

    response = post_payload
    handle_response(response)
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.warn "Failed to deliver webhook for bot #{bot.id} to #{bot.webhook_url} (#{e.class}: #{e.message})"
  end

  private
    def deliverable?
      bot.active? && bot.bot? && bot.webhook_url.present? && bot.rooms.exists?(message.room_id)
    end

    def post_payload
      uri = URI.parse(bot.webhook_url)
      request = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri)
      request["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
      request.body = payload.to_json

      Net::HTTP.start(
        uri.host,
        uri.port,
        use_ssl: uri.scheme == "https",
        open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT,
        read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT
      ) do |http|
        http.request(request)
      end
    end

    def handle_response(response)
      return unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK)

      reply_body = extract_reply_body(response)
      return if reply_body.blank?

      reply_message = message.room.messages.create!(body: reply_body, creator: bot)
      reply_message.broadcast_create
    end

    def extract_reply_body(response)
      raw = response.body.to_s.dup.force_encoding("UTF-8").scrub
      return if raw.blank?

      case response.content_type&.downcase
      when "text/plain"
        ERB::Util.html_escape(raw)
      when "text/html"
        raw
      end
    end

    def payload
      routes = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers
      room = message.room

      {
        event: "mention",
        author: {
          id: message.creator.id,
          name: message.creator.name
        },
        room: {
          id: room.id,
          name: room_name(room),
          reply_to: routes.room_bot_messages_path(room, bot.bot_key)
        },
        message: {
          id: message.id,
          body: {
            text: stripped_plain_text,
            html: message.body.to_s
          },
          link: routes.room_at_message_path(room, message)
        }
      }
    end

    def room_name(room)
      room.name.presence || room.users.without(bot).pluck(:name).to_sentence.presence
    end

    def stripped_plain_text
      return "" unless message.body.body

      sentinel = "__CAMPFIRE_MENTION_#{SecureRandom.hex(8)}__"
      replaced_fragment = message.body.body.fragment.replace("action-text-attachment") do |node|
        ActionText::Attachment.from_node(node).attachable == bot ? sentinel : node
      end

      ActionText::Content.new(replaced_fragment).to_plain_text
        .gsub(/[ \t\u00A0]*#{sentinel}[ \t\u00A0]*/) { |match|
          match.match?(/\A[ \t\u00A0]/) && match.match?(/[ \t\u00A0]\z/) ? " " : ""
        }
        .gsub(/\A[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+\z/, "")
    end
end
EOF

This is critical, because by creating a real HTTP socket, I can confirm that the `Net::HTTP.start` method functions as expected, as well as the headers, JSON body, `Content-Type: text/plain` or `text/html` headers, and the correct `204` response code.

My next step is to add this test to `test/models/bot/webhook_test.rb`. I'll employ a `TCPServer` listening on `127.0.0.1:0` to establish a local server, and then use `WebMock.disable_net_connect!(allow_localhost: true)` *within* that particular test to ensure it only allows localhost connections, with a `WebMock.disable_net_connect!` call in an `ensure` block to restore the standard behavior after the test is complete.

Finally, I will update `docs/bots.md` with some design notes, and then run the whole test suite along with RuboCop to make sure everything is perfect and conforms to coding standards.
